questions.questionHtml:
By interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be correct?

+ and –, 6 and 3
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

We have to find after interchanging the given two signs and numbers which of the following equation will be correct.

Given: + and –, 6 and 3

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) 8 – 3 × 4 ÷ 6 + 9 = 18

Given: + and –, 6 and 3

After interchanging the given two signs and numbers we get the;

⇒ 8 + 6 × 4 ÷ 3 - 9 = 18

⇒ 8 + 6 × 1.33 - 9 = 18

⇒ 8 + 8 - 9 = 18

⇒ 16 - 9 = 18

⇒ 7 ≠ 18

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 8 + 4 × 6 ÷ 3 – 9 = 15

Given: + and –, 6 and 3

After interchanging the given two signs and numbers we get the;

⇒ 8 - 4 × 3 ÷ 6 + 9 = 15

⇒ 8 - 4 × 0.5 + 9 = 15

⇒ 8 - 2 + 9 = 15

⇒ 17 - 2 = 15

⇒ 15 = 15

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 3) 9 ÷ 3 × 4 – 6 + 7 = 10

Given: + and –, 6 and 3

After interchanging the given two signs and numbers we get the;

⇒ 9 ÷ 6 × 4 + 3 - 7 = 10

⇒ 1.5 × 4 + 3 - 7 = 10

⇒ 6 + 3 - 7 = 10

⇒ 9 - 7 = 10

⇒ 2 ≠ 10

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) 6 ÷ 2 × 8 + 3 – 1 = 20

Given: + and –, 6 and 3

After interchanging the given two signs and numbers we get the;

⇒ 3 ÷ 2 × 8 - 6 + 1 = 20

⇒ 1.5 × 8 - 6 + 1 = 20

⇒ 12 - 6 + 1 = 20

⇒ 13 - 6 = 20

⇒ 7 ≠ 20

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

1 and 9
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Interchanging the given two numbers to find which of the following equation will be correct.

Let's check each option one by one:

Option 1) 9 × 3 – 4 ÷ 2 + 1 = 10

Given: 1 and 9

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ 1 × 3 – 4 ÷ 2 + 9 = 10

⇒ 1 × 3 - 2 + 9 = 10

⇒ 3 - 2 + 9 = 10

⇒ 12 - 2 = 10

⇒ 10 = 10

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 2) 1 + 9 × 3 – 4 ÷ 2 = 18

Given: 1 and 9

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ 9 + 1 × 3 – 4 ÷ 2 = 18

⇒ 9 + 1 × 3 - 2 = 18

⇒ 9 + 3 - 2 = 18

⇒ 12 - 2 = 18

⇒ 10 ≠ 18

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) 9 × 2 + 1 – 8 ÷ 4 = 12

Given: 1 and 9

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ 1 × 2 + 9 – 8 ÷ 4 = 12

⇒ 1 × 2 + 9 - 2 = 12

⇒ 2 + 9 - 2 = 12

⇒ 11 - 2 = 12

⇒ 9 ≠ 12

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) 9 – 1 + 6 ÷ 2 × 3 = 7

Given: 1 and 9

After interchanging the numbers we get the:

⇒ 1 – 9 + 6 ÷ 2 × 3 = 7

⇒ 1 - 9 + 3 × 3 = 7

⇒ 1 - 9 + 9 = 7

questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 

81 × 9 + 15 ÷ 3 – 4 = 50
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

Find which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct.

Let's check each option one by one.

Option 1) − and ×

Given: 81 × 9 + 15 ÷ 3 – 4 = 50

After interchanging the signs we get the;

⇒ 81 - 9 + 15 ÷ 3 × 4 = 50

⇒ 81 - 9 + 3 × 4 = 50

⇒ 81 - 9 + 12 = 50

⇒ 93 - 9 = 50

⇒ 84 ≠ 50

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) + and −

Given: 81 × 9 + 15 ÷ 3 – 4 = 50

After interchanging the signs we get the;

⇒ 81 × 9 - 15 ÷ 3 + 4 = 50

⇒ 81 × 9 - 5 + 4 = 50

⇒ 729 - 5 + 4 = 50

⇒ 733 - 5 = 50

⇒ 728 ≠ 50

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) ÷ and −

Given: 81 × 9 + 15 ÷ 3 – 4 = 50

After interchanging the signs we get the;

⇒ 81 × 9 + 15 - 3 ÷ 4 = 50

⇒ 81 × 9 + 15 - 0.75 = 50

⇒ 729 + 15 - 0.75 = 50

⇒ 744 - 0.75 = 50

⇒ 743.25 ≠ 50

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) ÷ and ×

Given: 81 × 9 + 15 ÷ 3 – 4 = 50

After interchanging the signs we get the;

⇒ 81 ÷ 9 + 15 × 3 – 4 = 50

⇒ 9 + 15 × 3 - 4 = 50

⇒ 9 + 45 - 4 = 50

⇒ 54 - 4 = 50

⇒ 50 = 50

⇒ LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
